title: Harness Lane Capability Profile
description: One harness lane's capability/posture evidence as data. The profile holds PROBE FACTS (what was verified, on which executable version and platform, by which method); routing eligibility is a separate, non-escalating projection owned by routing configuration — a routing artifact may never claim a more permissive posture than the profile evidence proves (SEM-R01/R02/R03). Evidence expiry is a VALIDITY CONDITION, not a stored boolean: this record is valid only while a live probe of the lane's executable matches the recorded executable_version + platform; consumers MUST fail closed on mismatch or unprobeable executables (SEM-VC01). Re-derivation produces a new immutable evidence record via a human-reviewed change; agents never self-clear a fence. This schema is tool-validated: portable core plus the constructs listed in the family README.

posture.description: Write-denial posture class, strongest to weakest: OS sandbox > tool deny-rules > none.

iso-date.description: Calendar date (UTC) the evidence was derived.

profile_schema.description: Exact canonical $id URI of this schema. Consumers MUST reject a profile whose profile_schema is missing or unknown (fail-closed; no version negotiation in v0).

lane.description: Harness lane identifier this evidence record describes.

platform.description: Platform the evidence was derived on (e.g. a process.platform value). Part of the validity-condition key.

executable_version.description: Executable version the evidence was derived against. Part of the validity-condition key: capability evidence expires with the CLI version.

version_resolution.description: Method by which the executable version was resolved (e.g. a --version probe of the PATH-resolved, symlink-resolved executable).

mechanism.description: How a caller-supplied schema is passed to the lane (flag + form), or null when the lane has no structured-output mechanism.

enforced.description: Whether the lane's own side enforces the schema. False means the supervising wrapper's independent validation is the whole gate.

control.description: Strongest write-denial control VERIFIED on this lane/version/platform. "none" means every probed control failed to deny writes.

mechanism.description: The concrete flags/configuration that implement the control. Null exactly when control is "none".

posture.description: Posture that results under the read-only reviewer default when the verified control is applied. In v0 this equals write_denial.control (enforced by the conditional blocks below); recorded separately so future control classes can project differently.

fenced.description: Contextual routing state REFERENCED, not owned: mirrors the routing fence at derivation time so the record is self-describing. Eligibility decisions live in routing; a profile cannot lift a fence, and agents never self-clear one.

fence_reason.description: Human-readable reason the lane is fenced. Required non-null when fenced, null otherwise.

method.description: How the capability facts were derived (e.g. a live capability smoke with positive/negative controls).

refs.description: Opaque references to the probe evidence (runlog digests, evidence-store keys, config anchors).

kind.description: The only validity-condition kind in v0: the record is valid iff a live probe of the lane executable yields exactly executable_version on exactly platform. Expiry is this runtime relation — never a stored boolean. Consumers MUST fail closed (treat the lane as posture "none"/ineligible) when the relation does not hold or cannot be probed.
